mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (المدثر): its origin is (المتدثر) [Translator's note: the printed text has «المندثر»]; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl because they share one point of articulation, and the dāl is stronger than the tāʾ [Translator's note: printed «الثاء»] because it is voiced (majhūra) while the tāʾ is unvoiced (mahmūsa). So both were turned into the stronger of them, since that is a strengthening of the letter; they were not turned into the tāʾ [printed «الناء»] because that would weaken the letter, since turning the stronger into the weaker is a deficiency in the letter and in the pronunciation. Such is the rule for most assimilation between two different letters: the weaker of them is turned into the sound of the stronger.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (ولا تمنن تستكثر): (تستكثر) is nominative because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do not give a gift in order to take more than it". It is also said that it is nominative because of the omission of (أن), the implied form being "Do not weaken, O Muhammad, from seeking much of the good"; when (أن) was omitted, it became nominative.
His saying (فإذا نقر في الناقور): [(في الناقور)] stands in the place of the one whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. It is also said [Translator's note: printed «وقبل», read as «وقيل»] that the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied and stands in the place of the agent.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (فذلك يومئذ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (يومئذ) is a badal (substitute) from it, and (يوم عسير) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (عسير) is a naʿt (adjective) of (يوم), and likewise (غير يسير) is also a naʿt of (يوم). It is also said that (يومئذ) is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (ذرني ومن خلقت): (من) is in the position of the accusative by conjunction with the nūn and yāʾ, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
His saying (وحيدا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied hāʾ in (خلقت), i.e. "I created him alone".
His saying (وجعلت له مالا ممدودا): (له) is in the position of the second object of (جعلت), because it means "made" (صيّرت) and takes two objects.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (وبنين شهودا): its singular is (ابن). The connective alif was dropped in the plural and the bāʾ took a vowel only because the plural returns a thing to its origin, and its origin is (بني) on the pattern faʿal. When it was pluralised it was returned to its origin, so they said (بنين). When the yāʾ, which is the final radical, took a vowel and what precedes it had fatḥa, [it turned into] an alif, and it was dropped because it was vowelless and the yāʾ of the plural after it was vowelless; and the letter before the yāʾ was given kasra according to the original pattern of the plural yāʾ in the accusative and genitive. It should properly have kept what precedes it with fatḥa, to indicate the departed alif, as they said (مصطفين) and (أعلين); but (ابن) ran in its weak-letter treatment in the singular contrary to analogy: it should properly have been like (عصا) and (رحى), with no connective alif entering it and its first letter not vowelless. So since it departed from its origin in the singular, it also departed in the plural from the principles of the weak-letter rules, because the plural is a branch after the singular. In the relative adjective (nisba) of it they said (بنوي), returning it to its origin; the origin of this wāw is an alif changed from a yāʾ, which is the final radical. Sībawayh allowed the nisba on its own wording, allowing (ابني), and others disallowed it.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying (وما أدراك ما سقر): the discussion of it has already preceded, since it is like (وما أدراك ما الحاقة).
His saying (ولا تذر): the wāw was dropped only because it was construed on its counterpart in usage and meaning, namely (تدع), since it has its meaning, and because no past tense is used from either of them. So (تذر) was construed on (تدع), and its first radical was dropped as it was dropped in (تدع). It was dropped in (تدع) only because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, since the fatḥa of the dāl is incidental: it took fatḥa only because of the guttural letter, and kasra is its origin; so the word was built on its origin and that was presumed in it, and the wāw of (تدع) was dropped for that reason. (تذر) was construed on it because it has its meaning and resembles it in that the past tense of both is not used.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His saying (لواحة): nominative with an implied "it is" (هي لواحة).
(سقر) is a diptote because it is a definite feminine noun.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (عليها تسعة عشر): (تسعة عشر) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (عليها) is the khabar (predicate). They are two nouns between which the conjunction was omitted and which contain it, so they were made indeclinable (mabnī) because they contain the meaning of the particle; they were made indeclinable on fatḥa because of its lightness. It is also said that they were made indeclinable on the fatḥa that belonged to the omitted wāw. Al-Farrāʾ allowed in speech making the ʿayn vowelless in the numbers from thirteen to nineteen.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (أصحاب): the plural of (صاحب) with the augment of (صاحب) dropped, as if it were the plural of (صحب), like (كتف) and (أكتاف).
His saying (ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا): if you make (ما) and (ذا) one noun, it is in the position of the accusative governed by (أراد). If you make (ذا) mean (الذي), then (ما) is an interrogative, a complete noun, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ذا) is the khabar (predicate); (أراد) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ذا) and the hāʾ is omitted from it, i.e. "What is that which Allah intended by this?", in the sense "What thing is that which Allah intended by this as an example?" (مثلا) is accusative as an explanation (bayān).
His saying (كذلك يضل الله من يشاء): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).
His saying (إنها لإحدى الكبر): it is not permissible to drop the alif and lām from (الكبر) and from what is like it, except (أخر), from which the alif and lām have been dropped while it contains their meaning, so it became definite by containing their meaning; that is why it is a diptote even in the indefinite. It is deflected (maʿdūl) from the alif and lām.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying (نذيرا للبشر): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (قم) in His saying (قم فأنذر); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. It is also said that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (إنها); also said: from (إحدى); also said: from (هو). It is also said that it is accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "Allah made it a warner", i.e. possessing warning, so the word is masculine by way of attribution (nasab). It is also said that it is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a warning possessing warning", so the word is masculine by way of attribution. It is also said that it is in the position of the maṣdar, i.e. "a warning to mankind", as He said (فكيف كان نكير), i.e. "My disapproval of them". [Translator's note: the source repeats part of this passage, apparently a copying error; translated as written.] It is also said that it is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying (وكنا نكذب) and (وكنا نخوض): the kāf was given ḍamma in this, and in the first letter of whatever is like it, such as (قمنا) and (قلنا), although the origin of all of it is fatḥa, so that the ḍamma would indicate that it was transferred from faʿala to faʿula. It is also said: it was given ḍamma only to indicate that it is among the verbs with wāw; and it is also said: to indicate that the dropped letter is a wāw. Both of these views fall away because they give kasra to the first letter of (خفت), which has wāw as its middle radical like (كان), and whose dropped letter is a wāw in the [verb of] choice, like the dropped letter of (قمت), (قلت) and (كنت). Their giving kasra to the first letter of (خفت) shows that they gave kasra only to indicate that it is from faʿila, with kasra on the ʿayn. As for their giving kasra to the first letter of (بعت), it is to indicate that it was transferred from faʿala to faʿila, and to indicate that it is among the verbs with yāʾ and that the dropped letter is a yāʾ. Because these reasons come together, ḍamma and kasra occur on the first letter of that; so know it.

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying (وما يذكرون إلا أن يشاء الله): the object of (يذكرون) is omitted, i.e. "they do not remember anything". (أن) is in the position of the accusative as an exception, or in the position of the genitive with the preposition implied. The object of (يشاء) is omitted, i.e. "unless Allah wills it".
